scenes.label: Meet the team
scenes.title: Find one enquiry
scenes.caption: Asha needs applicant ID sixty in a shuffled list of seven numeric practice IDs. Linear search can inspect them in order without sorting first. The team will count comparisons instead of declaring one method best for every task.
scenes.dialogue: How much work does this lookup actually take?

scenes.label: The problem
scenes.title: A fast-looking mistake
scenes.caption: A teammate proposes binary search on the shuffled list. Binary search discards part of the search range based on ordering, so that shortcut is not valid until the data satisfies the sorted-order requirement.

scenes.label: How it works
scenes.title: Compare with purpose
scenes.caption: Linear search checks items one by one. Binary search checks a middle item in sorted data and narrows the range. Sorting itself takes work. A tiny one-off enquiry and many repeated lookups can justify different choices.
scenes.dialogue: Count the work and state what you excluded.

scenes.label: Your decision
scenes.title: Protect the precondition
scenes.caption: The numeric IDs are still shuffled. Which action is justified before using binary search? Choose between using linear search directly and establishing the required sorted order before a binary-search experiment.
scenes.dialogue: Do not discard half a range without an ordering guarantee.

scenes.label: What changes
scenes.title: Measure the paths
scenes.caption: The supplied linear search finds sixty after five comparisons. On the sorted version, the supplied binary search finds it after two. Those lookup counts exclude sorting cost and do not prove that binary search is always the better overall choice.
scenes.dialogue: A lower lookup count is only part of the decision.

scenes.label: Enter the lab
scenes.title: Enter the logic lab
scenes.caption: Step through both searches, sort the practice cards before the binary run and choose a method for a new desk situation. Explain the sorted-data condition and whether preparation work is worth doing.
scenes.dialogue: Let us compare the whole task, not only its last step.
